subject: forter

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The implemented TAB order proceeds consecutively from the last brand card in the main content (label 15, Nordstrom brand card) to the first focusable item in the footer (label 16, Footer Forter logo link). In the navigation_order, implemented labels and inferred meaningful positions match exactly at 15 and 16. The screenshots show the brand-card row ending above a conventional footer area, with the footer logo appearing as the next visible focus target below the cards.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition should match this pattern when it moves from the last focusable element of one visible page region to the first focusable element of the next region, the two elements are adjacent in the observed keyboard sequence, no intermediate focusable controls are documented between them in navigation_order/KFG, and the destination begins a structurally distinct but expected continuation such as a footer.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed evidence shows a normal consecutive transition, not a ground-truth LNF. A possible detector error is that it treated crossing from main content into the footer as a semantic reordering signal, even though the supplied evidence shows direct adjacency and no skipped focusable elements. This cause is hypothetical; the detector's internal scoring is not provided.

This explanation is a hypothesis because no detector rationale is supplied.

subject_summary: This subject shows only false positives and no false negatives. Both FPs are directly observed, consecutive TAB transitions with matching implemented labels and inferred meaningful positions. The recurring characteristic is that the detector appears to have overflagged ordinary region changes near the end of main content and within the footer, even though the KFG and navigation_order document a clean linear sequence and the screenshots show plausible visual continuation.
